profile.summary: A Rewire study that tests variant scores on simulated rare-disease cases. Each case is one 1000 Genomes person's rare variants in the intellectual disability panel genes (PanelApp 285) plus one inserted ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant; a score succeeds when it ranks that diagnostic first. It compares established lookups (CADD, SpliceAI, REVEL, AlphaMissense), a ClinGen rule-based ranking, and added scores such as AlphaGenome AVI, GPN-MSA, GPN-Star and Evo 2.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How often a score, a combined model or a baseline ranks the inserted diagnostic variant first among a case's rare candidate variants (top 1). The primary question is whether adding AlphaGenome AVI to the combined lookups raises top 1 on 500 locked replication cases by at least 5 points.

quotes.text: A case is one 1000 Genomes person's rare variants in the panel's genes plus one inserted ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant. Each score ranks every variant in the case, and the outcome is where the diagnostic lands.

All figures are top 1 (the share of cases where the diagnostic variant ranks first), in percent, or gains in percentage points, with bootstrap intervals over people and a two-sided bootstrap p-value for each paired gain.
Top-1 of lookups plus AVI minus top-1 of lookups combined, both locked, on the 500, with the main
filter and the inheritance filter, with a paired 95% interval. The two models differ only by AVI.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Backgrounds are 1000 Genomes people's variants in the panel's MANE Select exons plus 20 bp, kept below 1% frequency, then filtered to grpmax below 0.1% using gnomAD v3.1.2 with the person and their family left out, and by the gene's mode of inheritance. ClinVar P/LP background variants are removed. Diagnostics are ClinVar P/LP variants with 2 or more review stars, drawn by class quotas. Three studies: 200 SNV cases and 120 indel cases on the first run's 50 people, and 500 replication cases on 50 new people with no diagnostic position reused. The median list on the 500 is 19 SNVs.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Models are cross-validated (5-fold, grouped by person) on the 200 and 120, and fitted once on the 200 and applied unchanged to the 500. The primary contrast has a 95% paired interval from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of people, read by a rule fixed in advance with a smallest gain of interest of 5 points; secondary scores use Bonferroni-adjusted intervals. A missing score ranks last. The README reports the primary gain as +1.8 points (-0.4 to +4.0), inside -5 to +5.

limitations.text: Simulated cases on short lists: 1000 Genomes people with an inserted diagnostic, median 19 SNVs on the 500 and 4 indels on the 120, one panel only.

quotes.text: After the filters the median list is 19 SNVs on the 500 and 4 indels on the 120. A real exome or genome has more candidates; these lists hold only rare variants in the panel's genes.
Their backgrounds hold no disease variant of their own, and the diagnostic is inserted, not observed.
on the intellectual disability panel only:

limitations.text: Diagnostics keep their full gnomAD frequency and most are absent from gnomAD, so a score that learned gnomAD presence could pick them for that reason.

quotes.text: Diagnostics keep their full gnomAD frequency by design, and most are absent from gnomAD (AC 0): 148 of the 200 (74.0%) and 386 of the 500 (77.2%).

limitations.text: ClinVar diagnostics were partly classified with the same lookup tools, which favours the lookups and both baselines; the lookups are near the ceiling at 90.6% top 1.

quotes.text: Many 2-star P/LP variants used PP3 evidence from these tools, and the PP3 thresholds were calibrated on ClinVar. That favours the lookups and both baselines.
At 90.6% top 1 (87.8 to 93.4) there is little room for any added score to gain.

run_guide.summary: Refetch the lookup scores and recompute the main results for the 500 replication cases with the study's benchmark script.
prerequisites: uv and Python 3.12, as the README's RUN alias states.

The first run's inputs in ../rare-disease/data/ (same repository), REVEL in ../../evo2-cloud-operations/data/raw/current-predictors/ and hg38 in ../../evo2-size-by-use-case/data/raw/hg38.fa.gz, as the README requires.
bcftools, tabix, samtools and curl for the shell scripts.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/rewire-bio/amp-2026-studies
cd amp-2026-studies
git checkout --detach 3fbab97b0f437972a1a6e0f2171ebb5d9a3d9f19
cd rare-disease-v2

steps.title: Compute results
steps.shell: uv run -q --python 3.12 --with-requirements requirements.txt python case_benchmark.py --study replication --analysis main
steps.explanation: The README shows case_benchmark.py with --study snv --analysis main and says every study runs with main; this uses the replication study.
